paper.title: Tangential Randomization in Linear Bandits (TRAiL): Guaranteed Inference and Regret Bounds

settings.name_in_paper: Linear bandits on sublevel sets of strongly convex functions (Assumptions 1-4)
unmapped: Action set is a sublevel set {g<=0} of a 3-times differentiable strongly convex g with bounded gradient/Hessian near candidate optimal actions and an alignment angle condition alpha_A < arctan(a_min/(n a_max))
Parameter set bounded away from origin: theta_min <= ||theta|| <= theta_max
The learner knows action-set geometry constants (a_min, alpha_A, gamma, m_varphi, n) to set the perturbation scale D and regulariser lambda
settings.definition_quote: Assumption 1: $\theta^\star \in \Theta$, where $\Theta$ is bounded, $\theta_{\min} > 0$... Assumption 2: $\varepsilon_t$ is zero-mean $M$-subgaussian... Assumption 3: $\Acal := \{x | g(x) \leq 0\}$ for a 3-times differentiable strongly convex function $g$...

settings.name_in_paper: Linear bandits on strongly convex sublevel sets with general noise (lower bound)
unmapped: Noise has a density p with finite positive Fisher information I_eps = E[(p'/p)^2]
Action set sublevel set of strongly convex g (Assumption 3 without alpha upper bound), plus Assumption 5: lambda_{n-1}(grad a*(theta)) >= lambda_C and differentiable eigen-decomposition of grad a*

algorithms.name: TRAiL (Tangential Randomization in Linear Bandits)
requires_knowledge_of: D (perturbation scale bounded by action-set geometry constants)

symbols.rho_t: M sqrt(n log((3+3 t a_max^2/lambda)/delta)) + sqrt(lambda) theta_max
symbols.c_0: geometric constant max{1/2 - sqrt(3)/4, 1/2 - sqrt(3) n a_max/varphi_g}

source.label: corollary_inference
source.quote: For all $(\delta,T)$ such that $F(\delta) \leq T$ and $\delta \in (0,1)$, $\probb{\bigcap_{t = F(\delta)}^{T} \left \{\vnorm{\hat{\theta}_{t + 1} - \theta^\star}^2 \leq \frac{ 2\rho_t(\delta)^2}{D c_0 \sqrt{t}} \right\}} \geq 1 - \frac{2\delta}{3}.$

results.notes: Parameter estimation error guarantee (inference), not regret; holds with probability >= 1-2delta/3 simultaneously over t.

tuning: perturbation variance D/sqrt(t) with D bounded as in Assumption 4

source.label: theorem_regret
source.quote: With $\lambda = \frac{8 n D^2}{\overline{m}_{\varphi}^{2} } (c_0 n + 1)$ for Algorithm \ref{alg:FELP}, $\probb{\mathscr{R}_{\theta^{\star}}(T) \leq  C \sqrt{T}  \log(T) } \geq 1 - \frac{1}{T}$ for sufficiently large $T$, where $C$ does not depend on $T$.

results.notes: Regret is defined via theta*^T(a* - a_t), i.e. pseudo-regret realised path, bounded with probability 1-1/T. C depends on n, geometry, M. Algorithm lists T as input data, but T is not used in the update; horizon marked known conservatively.

symbols.I_eps: Fisher information of the noise density, E[(p'/p)^2]

source.label: theorem_lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1, 3, and 5 hold. Then, for any policy $\pi$ and a large enough $T$,  $ \sup_{\theta^{\star} \in \Theta}  \E_{\theta^\star}^\pi\left[\mathscr{R}_{\theta^{\star}}(T)\right]\gtrsim  \sqrt{T/\mathscr{I}_{\ve}}$.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound via van Trees inequality; constants depend on lambda_C, alpha_A, c_3, n, prior. Theorem 13 (z^T V_T z <= R(T)/c_3 a.s.) is a supporting relation, not recorded separately.
